Romanian Poppy Seed Roll (Cozonac cu Mac)

Served at: Noaptea Lupilor

1 large roll (Serves 8-10)Prep 2 hours (plus rising time)Cook 45-55 min

While garlic is a central element in the traditions of Noaptea Lupilor (Night of the Wolves) on November 29-30, sweet baked goods offer warmth and comfort during this long, cold night. This rich, yeasted poppy seed roll, often referred to as a 'cake' in Eastern European contexts, provides a delightful treat to share with family as you reflect on the old traditions and ward off winter's chill.

Ingredients

  • For the Dough:
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm milk (about 105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, divided
  • 3 1/2 to 4 cups (420-480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • For the Poppy Seed Filling:
  • 1 cup (150 g) ground poppy seeds
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) honey
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) raisins (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • For the Egg Wash:
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 1 tablespoon milk

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 3 1/2 cups (420 g) of flour, the remaining granulated sugar, and salt.
  3. Add the activated yeast mixture, eggs, melted butter, vanilla extract, and lemon zest to the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, adding more flour a tablespoon at a time if the dough is too sticky, until it is smooth and elastic. Alternatively, knead in a stand mixer for 6-8 minutes.
  5. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. While the dough is rising, prepare the filling: In a saucepan, combine the ground poppy seeds, milk, sugar, and honey. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens (about 5-7 minutes).
  7. Remove from heat and stir in the raisins (if using), lemon zest, and vanilla extract. Let the filling cool completely before using.
  8. Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a large rectangle, approximately 12x16 inches (30x40 cm).
  9. Evenly spread the cooled poppy seed filling over the dough, leaving a 1/2-inch (1 cm) border on all sides.
  10. Starting from one long edge, carefully roll the dough tightly into a log. Pinch the seam to seal it and tuck in the ends.
  11. Carefully transfer the roll to a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let it rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  12. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolk and 1 tablespoon of milk for the egg wash.
  13. Brush the top and sides of the risen poppy seed roll with the egg wash.
  14. Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. If the top browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with aluminum foil.
  15. Remove from the oven and let the roll cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • Ensure your poppy seeds are finely ground; this creates a smoother, more flavorful filling. You can buy them pre-ground or grind whole seeds in a spice grinder.
  • For an extra rich dough, you can add 1-2 tablespoons of sour cream or plain yogurt to the dough ingredients.
  • This roll freezes well. Once completely cooled, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap and then in foil. Thaw at room temperature before serving.
